newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: J.P. Morgan Swiss unit puts Lusser on board.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan Swiss unit puts Lusser on board.

text.p: Former Swiss National Bank (SNB) head Markus Lusser has been elected chairman of the board of directors of J.P. Morgan (Suisse), the Swiss unit of the U.S.-based global investment bank, it said in a statment.
Lusser stepped down as chairman of the SNB governing board in April after reaching retirement age.

"His knowledge of business issues in Switzerland as well as the respect he commands in international financial circles will be a great asset to our firm," said William Oullin, head of J.P. Morgan's Geneva office.
J.P. Morgan (Suisse) is a wholly-owned Swiss bank unit of the group that was founded in 1981 and located in Geneva. It provides global financial services for individual investors.
The board of directors of J.P. Morgan (Suisse) is the bank's governing authority.
Lusser succeeded former Swiss ambassador Claude Caillat, who had served as chairman since 1985. The bank said Caillat remained a director of J.P. Morgan (Suisse).
Lusser was chairman of the three-man SNB board of directors from 1988 until this year.

He was also a member of the board of directors of the Basle-based Bank for International Settlements (BIS) from May 1988 to April 1996 and Swiss governor of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in Washington from 1992 to 1996. -- Zurich Newstoom, +41-1-631 7340
